title: The first few long words
description:
Write `std::vector<std::string> firstLongWords(std::string_view text, std::size_t minLength, std::size_t count)`.

It returns the first `count` words of `text` that have at least `minLength` letters. Words are separated by single spaces.

Build it as one lazy pipeline: `std::views::split(text, ' ')` cuts the text into pieces, `filter` keeps the long ones, `take` stops after enough have been found. Because views are lazy, the rest of the text is never even looked at once `take` has what it needs.

Each piece from `split` is a small range of characters; `std::string_view{ piece.begin(), piece.end() }` turns one into something you can measure and copy.
hints: Build `text | std::views::split(' ') | std::views::transform(toView) | std::views::filter(isLong) | std::views::take(count)`, where `toView` turns each piece into a `std::string_view`.
Loop over the pipeline and push each word into the result as a `std::string`.
